title: Checks for calls to Read::bytes on types which don’t implement BufRead.
summary: The default implementation calls read for each byte, which can be very inefficient for data that’s not in memory, such as File. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Lints subtraction between an Instant and a Duration, or between two Duration values.
summary: Unchecked subtraction could cause underflow on certain platforms, leading to unintentional panics. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks that there isn’t an infinite recursion in trait implementations.
summary: Infinite recursion in trait implementation will either cause crashes or result in an infinite loop, and it is hard to detect. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unsafe blocks and impls without a // SAFETY: comment explaining why the unsafe operations performed inside the block are safe.
summary: Undocumented unsafe blocks and impls can make it difficult to read and maintain code. Writing out the safety justification may help in discovering unsoundness or bugs. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for string literals that contain Unicode in a form that is not equal to its NFC-recomposition.
summary: If such a string is compared to another, the results may be surprising. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of unimplemented!.
summary: This macro, or panics in general, may be unwanted in production code. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: It detects references to uninhabited types, such as ! and warns when those are either dereferenced or returned from a function.
summary: Dereferencing a reference to an uninhabited type would create an instance of such a type, which cannot exist. This constitutes undefined behaviour. Such a reference could have been created by unsafe code. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for MaybeUninit::uninit().assume_init().
summary: For most types, this is undefined behavior. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for set_len() call that creates Vec with uninitialized elements.
summary: This is commonly caused by calling set_len() right after allocating or reserving a buffer with new(), default(), with_capacity(), or reserve(). It creates a Vec with uninitialized data, which leads to undefined behavior with most safe operations. Notably, uninitialized Vec<u8> must not be used with generic Read. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Detect when a variable is not inlined in a format string, and suggests to inline it.
summary: Non-inlined code is slightly more difficult to read and understand, as it requires arguments to be matched against the format string. The inlined syntax, where allowed, is simpler. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for passing a unit value as an argument to a function without using a unit literal (()).
summary: This is likely the result of an accidental semicolon. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for comparisons to unit.
summary: This includes all binary comparisons (like == and <) and asserts. Unit is always equal to itself, and thus is just a clumsily written constant. Mostly this happens when someone accidentally adds semicolons at the end of the operands. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Detects ().hash(_).
summary: Hashing a unit value doesn’t do anything as the implementation of Hash for () is a no-op. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for functions that expect closures of type Fn(…) -> Ord where the implemented closure returns the unit type.
summary: The lint also suggests to remove the semi-colon at the end of the statement if present. Likely, returning the unit type is unintentional, and could simply be caused by an extra semi-colon. Since () implements Ord it doesn’t cause a compilation error. This is the same reasoning behind the unit_cmp lint. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for a return type containing a Box<T> where T implements Sized
summary: It’s better to just return T in these cases. The caller may not need the value to be boxed, and it’s expensive to free the memory once the Box<T> been dropped. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for casts to the same type, casts of int literals to integer types, casts of float literals to float types, and casts between raw pointers that don’t change type or constness.
summary: It’s just unnecessary. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for #[cfg_attr(clippy, allow(clippy::lint))] and suggests to replace it with #[allow(clippy::lint)].
summary: There is no reason to put clippy attributes behind a clippy cfg as they are not run by anything else than clippy. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for Debug formatting ({:?}) applied to an OsStr or Path.
summary: Rust doesn’t guarantee what Debug formatting looks like, and it could change in the future. OsStrs and Paths can be Display formatted using their display methods. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for calls to TryInto::try_into and TryFrom::try_from when their infallible counterparts could be used.
summary: In those cases, the TryInto and TryFrom trait implementation is a blanket impl that forwards to Into or From, which always succeeds. The returned Result<_, Infallible> requires error handling to get the contained value even though the conversion can never fail. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for filter_map calls that could be replaced by filter or map.
summary: More specifically it checks if the closure provided is only performing one of the filter or map operations and suggests the appropriate option. Complexity. The intent is also clearer if only a single operation is being performed. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for find_map calls that could be replaced by find or map.
summary: More specifically it checks if the closure provided is only performing one of the find or map operations and suggests the appropriate option. Complexity. The intent is also clearer if only a single operation is being performed. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks the usage of .first().is_some() or .first().is_none() to check if a slice is empty.
summary: Using .is_empty() is shorter and better communicates the intention. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of fold when a more succinct alternative exists.
summary: Specifically, this checks for folds which could be replaced by any, all, sum or product. Readability. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks the usage of .get().is_some() or .get().is_none() on std map types.
summary: It can be done in one call with .contains()/.contains_key(). Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of .collect::<Vec<String>>().join("") on iterators.
summary: .collect::<String>() is more concise and might be more performant Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: As the counterpart to or_fun_call, this lint looks for unnecessary lazily evaluated closures on Option and Result.
summary: Using eager evaluation is shorter and simpler in some cases. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Detects functions that are written to return &str that could return &'static str but instead return a &'a str.
summary: This leaves the caller unable to use the &str as &'static str, causing unnecessary allocations or confusion. This is also most likely what you meant to write. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for .unwrap() related calls on Results and Options that are constructed.
summary: It is better to write the value directly without the indirection. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Suggests removing the use of a map() (or map_err()) method when an Option or Result is being constructed.
summary: It introduces unnecessary complexity. Instead, the function can be called before constructing the Option or Result from its return value. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Converts some constructs mapping an Enum value for equality comparison.
summary: Calls such as opt.map_or(false, |val| val == 5) are needlessly long and cumbersome, and can be reduced to, for example, opt == Some(5) assuming opt implements PartialEq. Also, calls such as opt.map_or(true, |val| val == 5) can be reduced to opt.is_none_or(|val| val == 5). This lint offers readability and conciseness improvements. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unnecessary calls to min() or max() in the following cases
summary: In the aforementioned cases it is not necessary to call min() or max() to compare values, it may even cause confusion. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Detects passing a mutable reference to a function that only requires an immutable reference.
summary: The mutable reference rules out all other references to the value. Also the code misleads about the intent of the call site. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for expression statements that can be reduced to a sub-expression.
summary: Expressions by themselves often have no side-effects. Having such expressions reduces readability. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of .map_or_else() “map closure” for Option type.
summary: This can be written more concisely by using unwrap_or_else(). Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Detects cases of owned empty strings being passed as an argument to a function expecting &str
summary: This results in longer and less readable code Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Disallow the use of rest patterns that don’t capture any fields.
summary: It might lead to unhandled fields when the struct changes. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of .map_or_else() “map closure” for Result type.
summary: This can be written more concisely by using unwrap_or_else(). Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for // SAFETY: comments on safe code.
summary: Safe code has no safety requirements, so there is no need to describe safety invariants. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the doc comments of publicly visible safe functions and traits and warns if there is a # Safety section.
summary: Safe functions and traits are safe to implement and therefore do not need to describe safety preconditions that users are required to uphold. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for imports ending in ::{self}.
summary: In most cases, this can be written much more cleanly by omitting ::{self}. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the presence of a semicolon at the end of a match or if statement evaluating to ().
summary: The semicolon is not needed, and may be removed to avoid confusion and visual clutter. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of Vec::sort_by passing in a closure which compares the two arguments, either directly or indirectly.
summary: It is more clear to use Vec::sort_by_key (or Vec::sort if possible) than to use Vec::sort_by and a more complicated closure. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for initialization of an identical struct from another instance of the type, either by copying a base without setting any field or by moving all fields individually.
summary: Readability suffers from unnecessary struct building. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for unnecessary calls to ToOwned::to_owned and other to_owned-like functions.
summary: The unnecessary calls result in useless allocations. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Suggests removing an unnecessary trailing comma before the closing parenthesis in single-line macro invocations.
summary: The trailing comma is redundant and removing it is more consistent with how rustfmt formats regular function calls. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for calls of unwrap[_err]() that cannot fail.
summary: Using if let or match is more idiomatic. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for calls to unwrap_unchecked when an _unchecked variant of the function exists.
summary: Calling the non-unchecked variant may result in checking that is then discarded if unwrap_unchecked is called directly afterwards, whereas the unchecked variant most likely avoids performing the check completely. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for private functions that only return Ok or Some.
summary: It is not meaningful to wrap values when no None or Err is returned. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for structure field patterns bound to wildcards.
summary: Using .. instead is shorter and leaves the focus on the fields that are actually bound. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for struct patterns that match against unit variant.
summary: Struct pattern { } or { .. } is not needed for unit variant. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for tuple and struct patterns with a wildcard pattern (_) is next to a rest pattern (..).
summary: The wildcard pattern is unneeded as the rest pattern can match that element as well. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unnested or-patterns, e.g., Some(0) | Some(2) and suggests replacing the pattern with a nested one, Some(0 | 2).
summary: In the example above, Some is repeated, which unnecessarily complicates the pattern. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of unreachable!.
summary: This macro, or panics in general, may be unwanted in production code. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Warns if a long integral or floating-point constant does not contain underscores.
summary: Reading long numbers is difficult without separators. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for deriving serde::Deserialize on a type that has methods using unsafe.
summary: Deriving serde::Deserialize will create a constructor that may violate invariants held by another constructor. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for imports that remove “unsafe” from an item’s name.
summary: Renaming makes it less clear which traits and structures are unsafe. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Warns if literal suffixes are not separated by an underscore.
summary: To enforce unseparated literal suffix style, see the separated_literal_suffix lint. Suffix style should be consistent. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for transmutes between collections whose types have different ABI, size or alignment.
summary: This is undefined behavior. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Checks for functions that are declared async but have no .awaits inside of them.
summary: Async functions with no async code create overhead, both mentally and computationally. Callers of async methods either need to be calling from an async function themselves or run it on an executor, both of which causes runtime overhead and hassle for the caller. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for trait method implementations that are declared async but have no .awaits inside of them.
summary: Async functions with no async code create computational overhead. Even though the trait requires the method to return a future, returning a core::future::ready with the result is more efficient as it reduces the number of states in the Future state machine by at least one. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Checks for uses of the enumerate method where the index is unused (_)
summary: The index from .enumerate() is immediately dropped. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Detects formatting parameters that have no effect on the output of format!(), println!() or similar macros.
summary: Shorter format specifiers are easier to read, it may also indicate that an expected formatting operation such as adding padding isn’t happening. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for unused written/read amount.
summary: io::Write::write(_vectored) and io::Read::read(_vectored) are not guaranteed to process the entire buffer. They return how many bytes were processed, which might be smaller than a given buffer’s length. If you don’t need to deal with partial-write/read, use write_all/read_exact instead. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for the creation of a peekable iterator that is never .peek()ed
summary: Creating a peekable iterator without using any of its methods is likely a mistake, or just a leftover after a refactor. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for calls to Result::ok() without using the returned Option.
summary: Using Result::ok() may look like the result is checked like unwrap or expect would do but it only silences the warning caused by #[must_use] on the Result. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Detects cases where a whole-number literal float is being rounded, using the floor, ceil, or round methods.
summary: This is unnecessary and confusing to the reader. Doing this is probably a mistake. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks methods that contain a self argument but don’t use it
summary: It may be clearer to define the method as an associated function instead of an instance method if it doesn’t require self. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for use Trait where the Trait is only used for its methods and not referenced by a path directly.
summary: Traits imported that aren’t used directly can be imported anonymously with use Trait as _. It is more explicit, avoids polluting the current scope with unused names and can be useful to show which imports are required for traits. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for unit (()) expressions that can be removed.
summary: Such expressions add no value, but can make the code less readable. Depending on formatting they can make a break or return statement look like a function call. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Warns if hexadecimal or binary literals are not grouped by nibble or byte.
summary: Negatively impacts readability. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for functions of type Result that contain expect() or unwrap()
summary: These functions promote recoverable errors to non-recoverable errors, which may be undesirable in code bases which wish to avoid panics, or be a bug in the specific function. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usages of the following functions with an argument that constructs a default value (e.g., Default::default or String::new).
summary: Readability. Using unwrap_or_default in place of unwrap_or/unwrap_or_else, or or_default in place of or_insert/or_insert_with, is simpler and more concise. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for .unwrap() or .unwrap_err() calls on Results and .unwrap() call on Options.
summary: It is better to handle the None or Err case, or at least call .expect(_) with a more helpful message. Still, for a lot of quick-and-dirty code, unwrap is a good choice, which is why this lint is Allow by default. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.
